I need a box, that is on the upside open. The outer dimensions are 220 x 300 x 160mm. The wall thickness should be 8mm and the bottom thickness 12mm | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Below is an exact, geometry-oriented recipe for creating the required open-top box with the available functions.  
(At this stage I am only describing what each function call will do; no code will be executed yet.)

STEP-BY-STEP PLAN  

1. Create the outer solid (the “blank”):
   • Call functions.block once with subtraction = False.  
   • Dimensions (x_size, y_size, z_size) = (220, 300, 160) [units: mm].  
   • Base-point (x, y, z) = (0, 0, 0).  
   • Result: a full rectangular prism that represents the maximal outside volume of the box.

2. Hollow out the interior, leaving all four walls 8 mm thick and the bottom 12 mm thick:
   • Call functions.block a second time with subtraction = True (because we are removing material).  
   • Wall thickness = 8 mm on X and Y faces, so reduce each lateral dimension twice that amount:  
     – Inner length  = 220 − 2·8 = 204 mm  
     – Inner width   = 300 − 2·8 = 284 mm  
   • Bottom thickness = 12 mm, so raise the inner block’s base-point by 12 mm in Z and give it a height of 160 − 12 = 148 mm:  
     – Inner height  = 148 mm  
     – Base-point (x, y, z) = (8, 8, 12)  
   • subtraction = True ensures this second block is cut out of the first, leaving an open cavity.

3. No cylinders, forces or other features are required, so no further function calls are necessary after the two block calls.

4. Finish with a single functions.finished call to confirm that all required functions have been called.

Once you tell me to proceed, I will supply the exact JSON-style arguments for the two functions.block calls (outer add / inner subtract) followed by the functions.finished call.
